text: Judith said: Listen to this plan, my friends. Take the head of Holofernes and hang it from the top of the town wall.

Then as soon as the sun comes up tomorrow morning, all of you strong men choose a leader for yourselves. Take your weapons and march out of town, as if you were going into the valley to attack the Assyrian guards on duty there.

When they see you, they will grab their weapons and run back to their camp and wake up their officers, who will rush to the tent of General Holofernes. They will panic when they find his dead body, and the entire Assyrian army will run from you in terror.
Then you and everyone else in Israel will kill them as they run away.

But before you do any of this, bring Achior the Ammonite here. I want him to see the head of the man who insulted the nation of Israel and who sent him to Bethulia to be killed along with the rest of us.
Achior was brought from Uzziah's house, and when he saw the head of Holofernes in the hands of one of the men, he fainted and collapsed on the ground.

Achior was helped to his feet, and at once he bowed down to show his respect for Judith. He said, “Every family in Judea thanks you, and I pray that all nations will shake with fear when your name is mentioned.
Please tell me how you did it.” Judith told Achior and the crowd everything that had happened from the day she left Bethulia until she returned.
As soon as she finished her story, the people of the town celebrated with shouts of joy.

After Achior had listened to what the God of Israel had done, he completely put his faith in God. Then he was circumcised and became an Israelite. And from that day on, he and his descendants worshiped God.
Early the next morning, the Israelites hung the head of Holofernes on the town wall. The men armed themselves with weapons, then went out in groups and stood on the hills around Bethulia.
As soon as the Assyrian guards saw what was happening, they reported it to their commanders, who made sure every Assyrian officer was alerted.

The highest-ranking officers went to Holofernes' tent and said to Bagoas, “You need to wake General Holofernes and tell him those Israelites had the nerve to march out of Bethulia to attack us. They may think we can be defeated, but we will wipe out every one of them.”
So Bagoas went inside and shook the curtain that separated Holofernes' bedroom from the rest of the tent. Bagoas waited, because he thought Judith was still with Holofernes.
No one answered, and so Bagoas opened the curtain and walked in. He saw the headless body of Holofernes lying on the floor,
and he began moaning and crying and tearing his clothes in sorrow.
Bagoas ran quickly to Judith's tent and saw that it was empty. Then he ran back out and shouted to the officers,
“We've been tricked. King Nebuchadnezzar's entire kingdom has been disgraced by one woman. Look! There's Holofernes lying dead on the ground—and his head is gone!”
As soon as the Assyrian officers learned what had happened, they tore their uniforms in sorrow. Loud crying and moaning was heard everywhere in camp.
